dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:4301.text: Something that ought not to occur. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “The sun or moon suffers an eclipse.” Formed from 月, with 又 indicating the sound. All characters in this group follow 有.

shuowen:4302.text: Having patterned ornament. Formed from 有, with 𡿿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4303.text: To possess together. Formed from 有, with 龍 indicating the sound. Read like 聾.

shuowen:4304.text: To illuminate. Formed from 月 and 囧. All characters in this group follow 朙.

shuowen:4305.text: The following day. Formed from 明, with 亡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4306.text: A lattice window opened to the light. Pictographic. All characters in this group follow 囧. Read like 獷. Attendant Jia says it is pronounced the same as 明.

shuowen:4307.text: The Rites of Zhou says: “When the state has doubts, make a covenant.” Feudal lords meet one another twice, with one covenant every twelve years. Facing north they address Heaven’s Directors of Vigilance and Destinies. For the covenant, they slaughter a victim and smear blood on their lips, using a red tray and jade vessel to set up the ox’s ear. Formed from 囧 and 血.

shuowen:4308.text: Evening. Formed from half-visible 月. All characters in this group follow 夕.

shuowen:4309.text: Resting: all under Heaven rest. Formed from 夕, with abbreviated 亦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4310.text: Not clear. Formed from 夕, with abbreviated 瞢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4311.text: To turn while lying down. Formed from 夕 and 卪; lying down has its joints or regulated postures.

shuowen:4312.text: Respectfully vigilant. Formed from 夕, with 寅 indicating the sound. The Changes says: “Vigilant at evening, as if in awe.”

shuowen:4313.text: Rain clearing at night so that stars appear. Formed from 夕, with 生 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4314.text: Distant or outside. Divination favors dawn; to divine now at evening is outside the proper business.

shuowen:4315.text: Diligent reverence. Formed from 丮, holding to one’s task: not resting even at evening is diligent reverence.

shuowen:4316.text: Still or lonely, 𡧯. Formed from 夕, with 莫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4317.text: Repeated. Formed from repeated 夕; 夕 succeeds another, hence “many.” Repeated 夕 makes 多; repeated 日 makes 曡. All characters in this group follow 多.

shuowen:4318.text: Qi calls “many” 夥. Formed from 多, with 果 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4319.text: Large. Formed from 多, with 圣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4320.text: The appearance of thick lips. Formed from 多 and 尚.

shuowen:4321.text: To pierce something and hold it. A single horizontal stroke pierces through, depicting valuables. All characters in this group follow 毌. Read like 冠.

shuowen:4322.text: A string of coins or shells. Formed from 毌 and 貝.

shuowen:4323.text: To capture. Formed from 毌 and 力, with 虍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4324.text: Contained, 嘾: plant flowers still unopened and enclosed. Pictographic. All characters in this group follow 𢎘. Read like 含.

shuowen:4325.text: A tongue. Pictographic; the tongue’s form is 𢎘. The text further says “𢎘 follows 𢎘,” which also indicates the sound; this repeated analysis is uncertain.

shuowen:4326.text: A tree producing shoots. Formed from 𢎘, with 由 indicating the sound. The Book of Shang says: “Like a fallen tree having 织枿”; the ancient text writes 由枿. The recorded phrase is uncertain.

shuowen:4327.text: Plant flowers flourishing, 甬甬. Formed from 𢎘, with 用 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4328.text: Plant buds flourishing. Formed from two 𢎘.

shuowen:4329.text: A tree with drooping flowers and fruit. Formed from 木 and 𢎘; 𢎘 also indicates the sound. All characters in this group follow 𣐺.

shuowen:4330.text: To bind. Formed from 𣐺, with 韋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4331.text: Plant fruits hanging down, 𠧪𠧪. Pictographic. All characters in this group follow 𠧪. Read like 調.

shuowen:4332.text: A tree. Formed from 木; because its fruit hangs down, it uses 𠧪.

shuowen:4333.text: The grain of a fine cereal. Formed from 𠧪 and 米. Confucius says: “𥻆 conveys the meaning of continuation.”

shuowen:4334.text: Grain and wheat sending out ears level at the top. Pictographic. All characters in the 亝 group follow 亝.

shuowen:4335.text: Equal. Formed from 亝, with 妻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4336.text: A tree’s thorn. Pictographic. All characters in this group follow 朿. Read like 刺.

shuowen:4337.text: Sheep jujube. Formed from repeated 朿.

shuowen:4338.text: Small jujubes growing in thickets. Formed from side-by-side 朿.

shuowen:4339.text: Split wood. Formed from half of 木. All characters in this group follow 片.

shuowen:4340.text: A split piece. Formed from 片, with 反 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4341.text: A split piece. Formed from 片, with 畐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4342.text: A writing board. Formed from 片, with 賣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4343.text: A writing slip. Formed from 片, with 枼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4344.text: Bed boards. Formed from 片, with 扁 indicating the sound. Read like 邊.

shuowen:4345.text: An opening through a wall with crossed wood forming a window. Formed from 片, 戶 and 甫. Tan Chang considers the element above 甫 to be 日, not 戶: a window lets one see the sun.

shuowen:4346.text: Short boards for building rammed-earth walls. Formed from 片, with 俞 indicating the sound. Read like 俞; alternatively like 紐.

shuowen:4347.text: A precious vessel with three legs and two handles for blending the five flavors. Long ago Yu collected metal from the nine regional governors and cast tripods beneath Mount Jing; entering mountains, forests, rivers and marshes, one would encounter none of the 螭, 魅 or 蝄蜽 spirits, thereby receiving Heaven’s blessings in harmony. In the Changes, Xun-wood below makes the 鼎 hexagram, depicting split wood for cooking. The large-seal script uses 鼎 for 貞. All characters in this group follow 鼎.

shuowen:4348.text: A tripod with a rounded, narrowed top. Formed from 鼎, with 才 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “鼐 tripods, 鼎 tripods and 鼒.”

shuowen:4349.text: An exceptionally large tripod. Formed from 鼎, with 乃 indicating the sound. The Lu Odes explanation says 鼐 is a small tripod.

shuowen:4350.text: A wooden bar passed across through a tripod’s handles to lift it. Formed from 鼎, with 冂 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “The temple gate admits seven large lifting bars.” This is the Changes’ “Jade lifting bars: great good fortune.”

shuowen:4351.text: To shoulder. Depicts cutting wood beneath a roof. All characters in this group follow 克.

shuowen:4352.text: Carving wood, 录录. Pictographic. All characters in the 录 group follow 录.

shuowen:4353.text: A fine cereal. It begins growing in the second month and ripens in the eighth, obtaining the seasonal mean, hence called 禾. Grain belongs to Wood: it grows when Wood rules and dies when Metal rules. Formed from 木 and abbreviated 𠂹; 𠂹 depicts its ear. All characters in this group follow 禾.

shuowen:4354.text: An imperial taboo: the personal name of Emperor Guangwu of Han.

shuowen:4355.text: The flowering ears and grain are 稼; the jointed stalks are 禾. Formed from 禾, with 家 indicating the sound. Another explanation: 稼 is household work. Another: crops in the fields are 稼.

shuowen:4356.text: Grain ready for harvest is called 穡. Formed from 禾, with 𠾂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4357.text: To plant. Formed from 禾, with 童 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4358.text: Early-sown crops. Formed from 禾, with 直 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Early and late crops, beans and wheat.”

shuowen:4359.text: Sown early but ripening late. Formed from 禾, with 重 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4360.text: Quick-ripening crops. Formed from 禾, with 坴 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Millet and grain, late- and early-ripening.”

shuowen:4361.text: Young grain. Formed from 禾, with 屖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4362.text: To plant densely. Formed from 禾, with 眞 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “Dense-grained and firm.”

shuowen:4363.text: Numerous. Formed from 禾, with 周 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4364.text: Dense. Formed from 禾, with 旣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4365.text: Sparse. Formed from 禾, with 希 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4366.text: A cereal. Formed from 禾, with 蔑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4367.text: A cereal. Formed from 禾, with 㣎 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4368.text: A cereal. Formed from 禾, with 厶 indicating the sound. In northern regions the owner of grain is called 私主人.

shuowen:4369.text: Rice with purple stalks, not sticky. Formed from 禾, with 糞 indicating the sound. Read like 靡.

shuowen:4370.text: The cereal 𪗉, foremost of the five grains. Formed from 禾, with 畟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4371.text: The cereal 稷. Formed from 禾, with 亝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4372.text: The sticky kind of 稷. Formed from 禾; 术 is pictographic.

shuowen:4373.text: The cereal 𪎭. Formed from 禾, with 祭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4374.text: Rice, 稌. Formed from 禾, with 舀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4375.text: Rice. Formed from 禾, with 余 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “Beef suits rice.”

shuowen:4376.text: In Pei state, rice is called 稬. Formed from 禾, with 耎 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4377.text: Nonsticky rice. Formed from 禾, with 兼 indicating the sound. Read like 廉 in 風廉.

shuowen:4378.text: A kind of rice. Formed from 禾, with 亢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4379.text: A kind of rice. Formed from 禾, with 毛 indicating the sound. Yi Yin says: “Among fine cooked grains are the grain of Mount Xuan and the 秏 of the Southern Sea.”

shuowen:4380.text: Awned grain. Formed from 禾, with 廣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4381.text: Rice shed this year that grows by itself next year is 秜. Formed from 禾, with 尼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4382.text: A distinct kind of grain. Formed from 禾, with 卑 indicating the sound. Langya has a county called 稗.

shuowen:4383.text: Grain plants leaning on one another. Formed from 禾, with 多 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a cereal name.

shuowen:4384.text: The tip of a grain plant. Formed from 禾, with 頃 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The grain ears hang luxuriantly.”

shuowen:4385.text: Qi calls wheat 䅘. Formed from 禾, with 來 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4386.text: Grain coming into ear, which people harvest. Formed from 爪 and 禾.

shuowen:4387.text: Grain with high-standing ears. Formed from 禾, with 勺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4388.text: The appearance of grain coming into ear, 𥝩. Formed from 禾, with 遂 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The grain ears hang luxuriantly.”

shuowen:4389.text: Grain hanging down. Formed from 禾, with 耑 indicating the sound. Read like 端.

shuowen:4390.text: Grain raising and sending out shoots. Formed from 禾, with 曷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4391.text: The awns of grain. Formed from 禾, with 少 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4392.text: The 穖 of grain, perhaps its awns; the self-referential gloss is uncertain. Formed from 禾, with 幾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4393.text: Two grains in one husk. Formed from 禾, with 丕 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “He sent down fine grains, black millet and double-grained millet.” These are Heaven’s fine grains bestowed on Hou Ji.

shuowen:4394.text: Grain swaying. Formed from 禾, with 乍 indicating the sound. Read like 昨.

shuowen:4395.text: To cultivate between grain plants. Formed from 禾, with 麃 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “They weed and mound the soil.”

shuowen:4396.text: To tread or roll over grain. Formed from 禾, with 安 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4397.text: To heap earth around the base of grain plants. Formed from 禾, with 子 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4398.text: To harvest and reap. Another explanation: to gather in a handful. Formed from 禾, with 齊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4399.text: To reap grain. Formed from 禾, with 蒦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4400.text: To pile up grain. Formed from 禾, with 資 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Pile it up in orderly heaps.”
